brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.

requirements.evidence: Full hex bases stacked at (0,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2), with half-west bases beside them at (1,0) on each level, so the cabinet is three storeys tall and two cells wide.

Three slide-style cell drawers: drawer:0#1,0#cut (level 0), drawer:1#1,0#cut (level 1), drawer:2#1,0#cut (level 2), one in each storey's half-base cell. check_build reports no errors and meshClash is clear.

finish.summary: A three-storey hex cabinet: a stack of three full bases with a half base beside each level, carrying three slide drawers, one per storey. Open faces are closed with caps and joints are bolted via lockJoints; check_build is clean with meshClash clear. I did not add props or doors. Structural strength and material suitability were not assessed; the configurator only checks fit.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
